full_judgment: 6. The respondent-defendant No. 1 con-tested the suit by filling written statement, stating, that, the banking business of East Bengal Mercantile Bank, Jamalpur wound up and the Bank leased out the entire suit property to defendant No. 1 Dr. Kudrat Ali-who firstly took settlement of 20 decimals of C.S. Plot No. 2058 under Khatian No. 255 at a yearly rental of Tk. 65 from Surandra Chowdhury, a director of the said Bank. Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 purchased 4 tin shed huts of that premises from the above director on 22nd Basaikh, 1358 B.S. at an amount of Tk. 400/-. After that defendant No.1 took settlement of another 20 decimals of land including the building thereon at a rental of Tk. 65 per annum through an Amalnama on 28th Baisakh, 1358 B.S. from the above director of the Bank. Since then the defendant No. 1 had possessed the suit property by exercising his own right, title and interest thereon and thus acquired good title by adverse possession also.
